_comment_logging: EF logs every SQL statement at Information; the job worker polls on a timer, so that alone produced ~150 lines/minute and buried real errors in `docker logs`. NOTE: every key inside LogLevel must be a valid log level — a comment there crashes startup.

Harbora._comment: MasterKey MUST be supplied via the HARBORA_MASTER_KEY env var in production (the installer generates it in deploy/.env). Left blank here so the app fails closed if it is missing.
Harbora._comment_proxy: TrustedProxyNetworks: comma-separated CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For headers are believed (the reverse proxy in front of the panel). Blank = Docker's private ranges. Widen this only to networks you control — it decides which IP the rate limiter and audit log record.

Jobs._comment_concurrency: MaxConcurrency: how many background jobs — deployments, backups, managed-service provisions, cron runs — this panel runs at the same time. Two jobs for the same target never overlap whatever this says. Leave it out to get 4, or the core count where that is smaller: a job here is usually a docker build on this same host. Set it to 1 to restore the one-job-at-a-time worker the platform ran before, which needs only a restart.

Monitoring._comment: Four operational numbers the collector and the monitoring dashboard used to carry as constants. All are left unset here so the code's defaults in MonitoringOptions.cs are the single source of truth — add a key to override one. DiskWarnRatio (fraction of disk in use before it counts as a problem) is read by three places that mean the exact same thing by it: the disk-warning alert, the home dashboard's Attention panel, and the monitoring page's own banner — raise it and all three agree. DiskAlertIntervalHours bounds how often the disk-warning alert may repeat for the same node. ThresholdRepeatAfterHours bounds how often a standing per-app threshold breach is reported again.
Monitoring._comment_backup_staleness: BackupStalenessHours is ONE of THREE backup-staleness numbers in this codebase, and they are not the same number wearing three hats — this setting changes only the first: (1) BackupStalenessHours (here, 48h default) — when the monitoring dashboard's own warning banner says a workspace's backups look stale. (2) Harbora.Infrastructure.Backups.VerificationSchedule.StaleAfter (7 days, a constant, NOT configurable here) — how long a stored restore-verdict is trusted before the platform re-verifies a backup by actually restoring it into a scratch database. (3) Harbora.Infrastructure.Tenancy.StorageMeasurer.StaleAfter (24h, a constant, NOT configurable here) — how long a volume's measured size is trusted for quota and billing before it is measured again. Collapsing these into one setting would silently change what the other two mean.

Retention._comment: How long each append-only table keeps its rows, in days (SweepHourUtc is an hour of the day, 0-23). Every key is listed with its shipped value in _comment_defaults below, and all of them are left unset here so the code's defaults are the single source of truth — add a key to override one. 0 or less means KEEP FOREVER, so a blanked value is harmless rather than a cutoff of 'now', and so is a number too large to be a date. A nightly sweeper applies these and never deletes a row a running operation still needs: an unfinished cron run (which is the runner's own lock), an in-flight node command, the database-access grant ledger, an unused reset link, or the build log of what an app is running right now. Idempotency records take no key at all — each row carries its own ExpiresAt.
Retention._comment_defaults: DeploymentLogDays 90, AuditLogDays 365, CronRunDays 90, NodeCommandDays 90, NodeEventDays 90, PasswordResetTokenDays 7, SweepHourUtc 3.
Retention._comment_policy: AuditLogDays is a POLICY decision, not a technical one. The default of 365 is a guess about YOUR obligations: if you are subject to a retention requirement (SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, a contract, a national record-keeping rule), set it deliberately rather than inheriting that guess. Nothing in the platform reads an audit row to decide anything, so a shorter value costs only your ability to answer questions about the past — and a longer one costs very little disk, because the audit trail is small next to the build logs.
Retention._comment_when: SweepHourUtc is the hour (UTC) the sweep runs at. The first pass on an install that has been running for a year is the largest DELETE this platform will ever issue, so put it somewhere quiet: a period counted from start-up instead would run it at whatever time the panel was last restarted.

Billing._comment: Pay-as-you-go billing is enabled by default. A new app/database prepays one running hour atomically with its creation; an empty or insufficient wallet is refused without persisting the resource. Once an hour has ended, every workspace is charged for what it held during it, and the creation line prevents the first hour being charged twice. A rate left blank is not free: creation is refused until it is priced. Set a rate to 0 only to mean deliberately free; even then the customer account must have a positive balance.
Billing._comment_backfill: MaxBackfillHours (default 72) bounds one catch-up after an outage: a panel that was down must not have hosted for free, but it must not decide on its own how much free hosting is acceptable either. Oldest hours are paid first and the NEWEST are the ones dropped, so an hour beyond the bound has not been billed yet and the next catch-up reaches it. Reaching the bound is always a warning naming the hours it left, never a silent skip. Three days covers a weekend outage while stopping a panel restored from an old backup issuing a month of bills in one pass.
Billing._comment_scheduler: When enabled, BillingScheduler persists one BillingRun per ended UTC hour and enqueues it on the durable Jobs table. A restart discovers missing hours oldest-first, and an accounting-incomplete hour is offered again without duplicating the lines already written. The first activation starts with the hour that just ended; it never bills the time in which billing was deliberately disabled.
Billing._comment_funding: There is no payment gateway. A provider administrator may credit a tenant directly, or create a single-use voucher whose plaintext is shown once and whose SHA-256 hash is stored. A workspace member redeems the code on /billing. Both paths append one idempotent Credit ledger line.
Billing._comment_env: deploy/docker-compose.yml maps BILLING_ENABLED, BILLING_CURRENCY and BILLING_MAX_BACKFILL_HOURS into these settings. BILLING_ENABLED defaults to true; set it to false only for a private installation that deliberately does not enforce balances.

Runtime._comment_retention: ImageRetentionCount: how many past versions keep their build image after a deploy. This is the real depth of instant rollback — beyond it a rollback must redeploy from source. 0 disables pruning (images accumulate forever).

Backups._comment_safety: EncryptArchives: encrypt artifacts (AES-GCM, key derived from the master key) before they leave staging — volume/database archives hold raw application data. SnapshotBeforeRestore: tar the current volume aside before a restore overwrites it, so a bad restore is itself recoverable.
Backups._comment_module: Backup module (docs/backup-sync/). Kopia drives a local repository only; S3-family repositories use the built-in engine, whose credentials stay encrypted end to end. RestoreRoot is the directory every restore destination must resolve inside.
Backups._comment_sources: AllowedSourceRoots is EMPTY on purpose: until it names directories, no directory can be backed up. A backup engine pointed at an arbitrary path is an arbitrary-file read with a download button on the end, so the default must not include /etc or Harbora's own key directory. Docker volumes need no allowlist — they are already this platform's own workloads — but they are copied into StagingDirectory by a helper first, which costs a temporary full copy on disk.

_comment_sync: Syncthing's own API is a direct path to every file it holds, bypassing Harbora's authentication — bind it to loopback or a private network only, never publish it. ApiKey belongs in an environment variable, not here. AllowedRoots is EMPTY on purpose: a sync folder is a directory this node both reads AND writes on a remote device's instruction, which is a stronger capability than backup's read.
_comment_features: Backup and Sync ship OFF. Enabling is a deliberate act after reading docs/backup-sync/MERGE_GUIDE.md — in particular, the Kopia CLI flags are written against a pinned release and should be exercised once against the installed binary first. EncryptedSyncNode is experimental.

Learning._comment: Where the Learning Centre's nine tutorial chapters live, relative to the content root (or a rooted path). docs/tutorial is correct for the container — the Dockerfile copies the chapters to sit next to the published DLL — and DependencyInjection.ResolveChaptersRoot falls back to walking up from the content root for a dev run, where that relative path does not exist.
